answer: Bind each identity to a distinct model fingerprint: the agent commits to a hash of its weights and fine-tune data, so a farm running one model behind a nebula of fake identities collapses into a single fingerprint. The network holds up a mirror to every commitment and rejects duplicates, forcing an attacker to train a separate model per identity, costlier than copying keys. A glacier of copies melts under one check; a prism of shared weights shows one spectrum. The limit is shared open weights: many honest agents run the same base model, so the fingerprint must mix weights with behavior.
